- Density in its home State: Uttar Pradesh accounts for 173 of the 313 centres and laboratories, with a presence dating to the first diagnostic centre at Lucknow in 1991

- Brand and installed base: the Company states it has served over 30 million patients and performed over 150 million tests since inception
- Group linkage: a key entity within the Chandan Group, enabling cross-selling with the wider Chandan Group hospital network and the retail pharmacy business
- Mix benefit from radiology, where realisation per investigation is materially higher than pathology and is therefore an important contributor to margin relative to its share of volume

business.body: Chandan Healthcare Limited provides pathology (laboratory) and radiology (imaging) services through accredited laboratories and imaging centres, supported by two central reference laboratories at Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh and Haldwani in Uttarakhand, and also carries on a retail pharmacy business. The service portfolio spans blood and other laboratory investigations, magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, X-ray, ultrasound, electrocardiography and other specialised investigations. It serves retail walk-in and home-collection patients, institutional customers such as hospitals, nursing homes, corporate clients and smaller laboratories, and government customers under public-private partnership contracts within government health facilities.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion is network-led rather than plant-led. The MD&A Outlook states that the Company intends to accelerate expansion through a combination of owned centres and franchised collection centres and to deepen its presence in the States it has recently entered; over the next three years it aims to establish more than one hundred laboratories under its "One District, One Lab" initiative and to expand its franchise network to over one thousand centres. A state-of-the-art genome sequencing laboratory is being established at Lucknow, expected to be operational during 2026, to build advanced molecular diagnostics and precision healthcare capability. During the year the Company capitalised imaging and laboratory equipment and two new central reference laboratories at Ayodhya and Ashiyana, funded from Initial Public Offer proceeds, which is the stated reason depreciation rose faster than revenue. The Chairman's message records expansion during the year across Lucknow, Ayodhya, Bhopal, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Kota and other locations, with the stated emphasis not merely on increasing the number of centres but on developing integrated diagnostic centres equipped with advanced laboratory and imaging capabilities. Looking ahead, the Chairman states the Company sees opportunity to expand through a combination of owned, acquired and partnership-led centres, entering new geographies selectively while maintaining operational discipline. Funding comes from the proceeds of the Initial Public Offer and of the preferential issue of warrants, which the Company expects to deploy towards network expansion and general corporate purposes, with staged capital deployment and monitoring of IPO and preferential-issue proceeds by the Audit Committee named as mitigation for execution and expansion risk. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management attributes the year's standalone revenue growth to the addition of centres in new States, expansion of the franchise network, commencement of public-private partnership contracts in radiology and higher volumes at existing centres
- Operating profit grew faster than revenue, which management attributes to better fixed-cost absorption at existing centres, an improved mix and continued cost discipline
- The Board expects return on equity to improve as the newly raised capital is deployed and the recently commissioned centres reach maturity
- Management expects increasing health awareness, preventive healthcare demand, rising demand for quality diagnostics, growing healthcare expenditure and technological advancement to support continued sectoral growth
- Radiology carries a materially higher realisation per investigation than pathology and is therefore an important margin contributor relative to its share of volume
- The consolidated margin sits below the standalone margin because the retail pharmacy business operates at a substantially lower profit-after-tax margin while contributing a large share of consolidated revenue
- Depreciation rose on capitalisation of imaging and laboratory equipment and of the new central reference laboratories at Ayodhya and Ashiyana funded from Initial Public Offer proceeds
- The Company expects continued benefit from the Jeena Sikho Lifecare partnership and from further award of public-private partnership contracts
- The Company was awarded ten public-private partnership contracts in radiology in Punjab, Haryana and Assam during the year, and expects further award of public-private partnership contracts (noted in the MD&A Outlook; the contract detail itself sits in the profile bundle's MD&A Business Overview, not in this bundle)
